\sphinxAtStartPar
The legacy Matlab \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{randraw.m}} surface has been retired. Probability distributions now live in the C++ API as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::distr}}, available directly from:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/pluss.h\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This manual is organized around how users actually consume the layer:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
start with \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{quickstart}} for the short\sphinxhyphen{}path workflow

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{api\_reference}} when you need the function surface

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{distribution\_catalog}} when you need names, aliases, and parameter conventions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{build\_outputs}} when you want to build the docs or the example binary locally

\end{itemize}

\chapter{Quickstart}
\label{\detokenize{quickstart:quickstart}}\label{\detokenize{quickstart::doc}}

\section{Include Path}
\label{\detokenize{quickstart:include-path}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+cp}{\PYGZsh{}}\PYG{c+cp}{include}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{c+cpf}{\PYGZlt{}pluss/pluss.h\PYGZgt{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The distribution layer is exposed as \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::distr}}. No extra include is needed when PlussMa is part of the build.

\PYG{+w}{    }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Config}\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}dtype}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{ScalarType}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{Float32}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}platform}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{pCPU}\PYG{p}{)}
\PYG{+w}{        }\PYG{p}{.}\PYG{n}{with\PYGZus{}pinned}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{n+nb}{true}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{gamma\PYGZus{}like}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{distr}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}like}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{gamma}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p}{\PYGZob{}}\PYG{l+m+mf}{2.0}\PYG{p}{\PYGZcb{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{like}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}
\PYG{k}{auto}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{signs\PYGZus{}like}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{=}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{pluss}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{distr}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{o}{:}\PYG{n}{sample\PYGZus{}like}\PYG{p}{(}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{rademacher}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{p}{,}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n}{like}\PYG{p}{)}\PYG{p}{;}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample\_like(...)}} preserves the visible tensor contract from \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{like}}: shape, dtype, and platform. It also forwards the pinned flag into the sampling config, but the current runtime does not surface pinned\sphinxhyphen{}memory state through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{is\_pinned()}} yet.

\section{Intended Style}
\label{\detokenize{quickstart:intended-style}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The user\sphinxhyphen{}facing model is:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
keep everything under \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{pluss::distr}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
pass the distribution name plus a short parameter list

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
let \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sample\_like}} carry shape and dtype when you already have a target tensor

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
stay on \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} throughout instead of bouncing between helper wrappers

\end{itemize}

\sphinxstepscope

Samples a new \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Series}} from the chosen family. Use the parameter list required by that distribution, pass the output shape through \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{sizes}}, and use \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{cfg}} when you need to control dtype or platform.

\label{\detokenize{api_reference:id3}}
